correctness.rationale: A class in degree-six H3=K3^3 must have induced minimum degree 3. The neighborhood of each vertex is three disjoint K2 edges; common-neighbor counts for distinct vertices are at most two, and all triangles are coordinate lines. This rules out sizes 1–5 (including parity argument for any hypothetical size-five class), so 27 vertices allow at most floor(27/6)=4 colours. A six-vertex feasible induced subgraph cannot have degree four or five; it is cubic, hence a triangular prism or K3,3. K3,3 would require three common neighbours, impossible, while prism triangles are parallel coordinate lines, yielding exactly 3 choices for full coordinate times 2 for partial coordinate times 3 fixed symbols times C(3,2)=54 rectangles. Fresh independent exhaustive enumeration of all C(27,6)=296010 six-subsets found exactly 54 such sets. The explicit 3x3 four-colour table has at least one same-colour row/column neighbor plus two same-colour third-axis neighbours at each of 27 points, proving 4 colours. Product colouring with H2 factors yields 4*3^r nonempty classes with 3+2r same-colour neighbors out of 6+4r in each dimension 2r+3, all r>=0. The product claim is algebraic for all r; separate checks at dimensions 3,5,7 are only bounded corroboration.
residual_risks: The bound in odd dimensions >=5 is a lower bound only, not optimality or classification of optimal colourings.
Six-vertex classification concerns only minimal admissible classes, not all classes in a valid partition.
